title: SkailrExpertProfile
description: YAML frontmatter of a minted expert profile at .claude/experts/profiles/<slug>.md. Authoritative machine sidecar for contract expert-profile-format v1. Logical schema id: skailr.expert/v1.
$comment: Kept inside a hand-walkable subset of draft 2020-12 (type, required, properties, enum, const, pattern, minLength, minItems, minimum, items, additionalProperties, default) because this repo has zero runtime dependencies and check-experts.mjs must validate without a JSON Schema library. Cross-field rules are NOT encoded here: see the Cross-field rules note below.

schema.description: Schema tag. A profile without this exact value fails validation (check-experts rule 1).

slug.description: Expert identity. Must equal the profile filename stem. The mandatory -expert suffix guarantees no collision with existing pack role names (brief A9).
slug.$comment: The reserved pack role names `expert` and `expert-scout` do not match this pattern, so they can never be minted as slugs. check-experts rules 4, 5, 6, 7.

name.description: Human-readable expert name. Also the profile body H1.

classification.description: Closed three-value enum (brief A7). internal: depth sourced from this repo. external: depth sourced from the field beyond the repo, and requires .claude/experts/research/<slug>.md. hybrid: requires both an internal and an external source set.

route_when.description: The single sentence routing reads to decide whether an ask falls in this expert's band. Sharp and specific, in the voice of .claude/teams/registry.md route-when lines.
route_when.$comment: A route_when shorter than 30 characters is a check-experts WARNING (weak proxy for a vague band), not a schema error. Band overlap between experts is explicitly not mechanically checkable (brief A11).

depth.description: The dual-depth non-negotiable made machine-readable. Both dimensions are required for every expert, including internal ones.

industry.description: Field/vertical topics. Non-empty even for an internal expert: it still carries field depth about the domain the repo operates in.

repo.description: Subsystems, directories, or capabilities of this project that this expert knows concretely.

sources.description: What makes every claim in the profile auditable. An uncited claim is a protocol violation (brief risk 6).

kind.description: repo-path refs must exist on disk. url and doc refs are what make an external claim auditable.

ref.description: Repo-relative path, URL, or doc identifier.

note.description: What this source supports. Required so a reader can tell which claim rests on which source.

maturity.description: Living-artifact lifecycle (brief A8). provisional is the state every auto-minted expert starts in and can advise and co-author but never gate bindingly. established requires explicit human action. deprecated experts are never dispatched and are retained for history.

gate.description: Per-expert gate participation, defaulting to the project gate_mode. Narrows but never widens gate_mode: with gate_mode soft, gate hard is still advisory.
gate.$comment: gate: hard is only valid with maturity: established (check-experts rule 16).

minted.description: Provenance of the mint. Every mint has an auditable trigger; there is no ambient minting.

by.description: The trigger that minted this expert: T1 explicit /mint-expert, T2 the /map-repo phase after the confirm gate, or T3 the build-command consult step.

basis.description: The signal that justified this mint, concretely enough to audit against the mint_threshold.

last_reviewed.description: Enables git-based staleness detection instead of a timer (brief A26).

against_sha.description: Git sha at review time. When a cited repo-path source has changed since this sha, callers post a refresh heads-up.
against_sha.$comment: The literal `unknown` is permitted so a mint in a non-git working tree is not blocked. Staleness detection is skipped, not failed, for `unknown`.

supersedes.description: Slug of a retired expert this one replaces, or null. A non-null value naming a slug that does not exist fails validation (check-experts rule 19).

x-cross-field-rules.$comment: Documentation only, not evaluated. These are mechanically checkable but are deliberately implemented in scripts/skailr/check-experts.mjs rather than encoded as if/then/allOf, because the validator hand-walks this schema without a JSON Schema library. Rule numbers refer to contract expert-validation-gate v1.
rules: 10: every sources[] entry with kind repo-path has a ref that exists on disk
11: classification internal requires at least one repo-path source
12: classification external or hybrid requires at least one url or doc source
14: classification hybrid requires both an internal and an external source set
5: slug must equal the profile filename stem
6: slug must be unique across profiles
7: slug must not collide with a reserved pack role name
17: the profile body ## Known limits section must be non-empty
18: no required profile body section may be missing
19: a non-null supersedes must name an existing slug
